objective_for_doctor: A 7-year-old Male patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have a fever, swollen or painful lymph nodes, and exhausting pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi doctor. I’ve had a fever and my lymph nodes feel swollen and painful. I also feel really exhausted with bad pain in my head (back, top, and forehead) and I have pain in my mouth/gums and in my groin area (right and left labia majora), plus some sores on my skin and my right inner cheek.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—how high has the fever been and how many days has this been going on? Also, have you noticed any sore throat or trouble swallowing, and are the skin sores blister-like or ulcer-like?

My fever has been up, but I don’t know the exact number. It started kind of fast and I’ve been feeling like this for a few days. I don’t have a sore throat or trouble swallowing. The skin sores look more like ulcer-like spots rather than blisters.

Doctor: Thanks—next, do the mouth/gum pain and inner-cheek sores look like white/yellow ulcers, and have you noticed any swollen neck nodes only or also groin nodes with redness in the area? Also, has anyone at home had similar illness or known chickenpox/HSV recently?

The mouth/gum pain is there, and the sores in my inner cheek look like ulcer-type spots—kind of pale/whitish or yellowish. I have swollen painful lymph nodes in more than one area, including groin, and the skin area there looks red. No one at home has had the same illness, and I don’t know of anyone with chickenpox or HSV recently.

Doctor: I’m concerned about a disseminated viral process (like herpes/HSV) or other infection causing mouth ulcers + painful generalized lymph nodes—can you tell me if your skin/inner-mouth sores started within 1–3 days of the fever and whether you have burning/tingling before they appeared? Also, have you had any difficulty peeing, severe testicular pain, or a painful swollen area in the groin (like a boil)?

The skin and inner-mouth sores seemed to start pretty close to the fever—within a few days. I don’t remember any burning or tingling before they appeared. I haven’t had trouble peeing, severe testicular pain, or a painful swollen boil-like spot in the groin.

Doctor: Given fever plus widespread painful ulcer-like mouth lesions and ulcer-like skin lesions with generalized tender lymph nodes (including groin) in a 7-year-old, I want to rule out disseminated HSV and other serious infections. REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_diff, CMP; REQUEST TEST: Herpes_Simplex_Virus_PCR_from_swab_of_mouth_or_skin_lesion; REQUEST TEST: Varicella-Zoster_Virus_PCR_from_lesion; REQUEST TEST: HIV_test (age-appropriate, provider-guided) and consider Blood_culture if still febrile.  
Doctor: While tests are pending, do you have any eye pain/redness or vision changes, and are you able to drink/keep fluids down despite the mouth pain?
I don’t have eye pain or redness, and I haven’t noticed any vision changes. I can drink some, but the mouth pain makes it hard to keep enough fluids in.

Doctor: Thank you—since fluids are hard to keep down and lesions are ulcer-like in mouth and skin with tender nodes in groin too, I’m worried about disseminated HSV/other serious infection rather than a simple viral cold. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis_and_urine_culture, REQUEST TEST: CRP_and_ESR; if oral intake is poor, we’ll also consider IV fluids and urgent clinician reassessment.
Okay doctor. I can try to drink, but it’s really painful in my mouth so I’m not getting much. If you need to check my urine and do blood tests, that’s fine.

Doctor: I’m going to make sure there isn’t severe dehydration or a bloodstream infection—REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis_and_urine_culture and REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_diff, CRP_and_ESR, and start IV fluids if you can’t drink enough.  
Doctor: While we check results, I need one quick safety question: do you have any trouble breathing, swallowing saliva, or are you very sleepy/confused compared with usual?  
Doctor: If yes, we treat this as urgent and escalate immediately; if no, we’ll focus on disseminated HSV/other serious causes based on PCR results from your mouth/skin lesions.
I don’t have trouble breathing or swallowing my saliva. I’m very sleepy and exhausted, but I’m not confused compared to usual.

Doctor: Thank you—because you’re very sleepy/exhausted and you can’t drink much, I want you assessed urgently in person for possible dehydration and serious infection while we await labs/PCR. REQUEST TEST: Point-of-care_vitals_and_oxygen_saturation, and I’m also asking the team to start IV fluids now and give pain control.
Okay. I agree—I’m really tired and it’s hard to drink because my mouth hurts, so you can check my vitals and start IV fluids and pain medicine.

Doctor: I’m going to assume urgent evaluation is happening now. Can you tell me whether you’ve had **rash on hands/feet**, **any genital lesions**, or **any history of eczema/skin breaks**?

Doctor: Also, do your ulcers look like **punched-out lesions** and are the lymph nodes **very large/firm** or just tender?

I don’t have a rash on my hands or feet that I know of. I do have sores on my groin area (right and left labia majora). I don’t know about eczema or skin breaks before.

The mouth and skin ulcers look kind of “punched-out” to me. The lymph nodes feel swollen and painful, but I wouldn’t say I know if they’re very large or firm—more like tender and swollen.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Herpes Simplex Virus (primary or reactivation HSV) causing widespread mucocutaneous ulcerative lesions with generalized tender lymphadenopathy (serious illness—needs urgent IV fluids/acyclovir pending PCR).
